title: Aurora Postmortem & Incident Follow-up
summary: Postmortem review of 2025-11-18 incident: intermittent latency spikes and 5xx errors affecting Aurora's production inference traffic. Discussed root cause (autoscaler + driver mismatch causing quantized kernel failures), mitigations deployed (hotfix rollback, node pinning), longer-term reliability improvements (preflight driver checks, stronger canary policies, EV cache tuning) and next steps for benchmarks and security review.
next_steps: Redwood to share postmortem doc and extended logs (Jordan) — by 2025-11-22
SE to run 20% traffic canary with driver pinning and report perf delta (Priya) — by 2025-11-24
Aurora to provide sample failing request IDs and SLO targets (Michael) — by 2025-11-21
Schedule technical deep dive on KV cache eviction behavior (Priya + Nadia) — schedule by 2025-11-25
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Avery Gomez (CSM), Michael Chen (Aurora SRE), Sara Alvarez (Head of Infra), Liam O'Connor (Security), Nadia Patel (Platform), Tom Reynolds (Eng Lead)

Summary (auto): quick recap of outage on 2025-11-18, timeline and actions.

[00:00] Jordan: hi everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do a quick postmortem and then walk through next steps. michael, do you want to start with impact?
[00:12] Michael: yeah thanks jordan. on the 18th starting around 02:10 UTC we saw latency spikes and a rise in 5xxs for about 45 minutes, roughly 12% of requests affected. main customer-facing app saw slow downs, some timeouts. SLOs were breached briefly.
[00:30] Sara: our paging kicked off, we routed traffic off to a backup region which helped but there were still degraded responses for some users.
[00:42] Priya: can you confirm whether it was a particular model or route? uncertainty about a specific endpoint causing cache thrash?
[00:50] Michael: it was mostly the chat-generation route using prod-large-quant. we also saw higher-than-usual KV cache evictions around the same time.
[01:05] Tom: there's also a note that our autoscaler did a rolling cycle and some nodes came up with a new driver set after an infra update. could be related.
[01:20] Jordan: that's consistent with our preliminary RCA: some nodes were provisioned with CUDA/cuDNN versions that didn't match the quantized kernel build we were running, leading to a kernel fallback path that failed under heavy concurrent prefix cache usage.
[01:40] Liam: from security side, did any logs indicate data leakage or access anomalies?
[01:46] Michael: no evidence of data exfil, this was compute-level mismatches, not auth. logs show internal errors and gpus going unhealthy, not auth failures.
[01:58] Priya: to explain for context — when a quantized kernel encounters an ABI/driver mismatch it can throw errors or silently degrade performance. combined with the KV cache eviction pattern we saw a cascade: eviction spikes -> more work to rebuild KV cache -> longer sequences leading to different kernel paths -> increased latency and a subset of 5xxs.
[02:25] Jordan: sorry to interrupt, on our side we pushed a hotfix: we rolled back the autoscaler policy and pinned the driver versions for the affected pool, and we also enabled a fallback model variant with compatible kernels so customers saw reduced errors. that mitigated the immediate user impact.
[02:45] Nadia: did the fallback cause any output regressions? we observed some tokenization oddities in a small percentage.
[02:52] Priya: yes small regressions — a few prompts produced slightly different formatting. we tracked that to model variant differences rather than data corruption.
[03:05] Michael: timeline question — how long between detection and mitigation?
[03:09] Jordan: detection to rollback was about 22 minutes; full traffic normalization took ~40 minutes.
[03:18] Tom: we flagged that our canary windows were too short and the autoscaler churn was higher than expected during the deployment.
[03:30] Sara: also the node provisioning didn't include a preflight driver check; that might have caught the mismatch.
[03:40] Priya: agreed, suggestion: preflight driver compatibility check in provisioning, and a driver pinning policy in the orchestration layer for quantized workloads.
[03:55] Michael: also, is there a way to more gracefully degrade to CPU or a safe model variant without causing tokenization or formatting changes?
[04:05] Priya: we have graceful fallback logic but it needs better alignment on model families to avoid content drift; we can improve model variant alignment and a validation step that runs unit prompts to check regressions on failover.
[04:25] Liam: from compliance perspective we need the audit trail of the changes and confirmation that no PII was exposed. can we get a redwood log bundle?
[04:34] Jordan: yes we'll include the audit logs and the operator actions; we'll redact anything PII but include request IDs and timestamps.
[04:42] Avery: will add that to the postmortem doc.
[04:47] Michael: do you have metrics on how many requests hit the fallback model?
[04:51] Jordan: approx 14% of requests for that route.
[04:55] Tom: let's dig into the KV cache behavior — was the eviction threshold too aggressive? we saw a workload spike but not beyond expected capacity.
[05:05] Priya: initial analysis: the eviction threshold was tuned for median workloads; the spike pattern had many concurrent long-prefix requests which increased memory pressure and triggered eviction earlier. also, continuous batching increased memory footprints per GPU.
[05:25] Sara: so batching + long sequences + driver fallback equals perfect storm.
[05:30] Priya: exact.
[05:35] Jordan: mitigation list recap — 1) rolled back autoscaler and pinned drivers, 2) enabled safe model fallback, 3) flagged canary and provisioning checks. longer term — preflight driver check, stronger canary policies with small traffic ramp, KV cache eviction tuning and telemetry improvements, and a runbook for detection.
[06:00] Michael: for KV cache tuning can you recommend target sizes or eviction policies?
[06:06] Priya: we can propose conservative cache sizes for your profile and also adaptive thresholds based on observed prefix length histograms; we'll share a suggested config.
[06:20] Nadia: we also want to make sure KMS keys and audit logs for private deployments weren't affected; we are on Private deployment in a VPC. any differences there?
[06:30] Jordan: Private deployments use customer-managed networking but the same runtime; driver mismatches can still occur if clusters are upgraded without preflight checks. for Private we recommend an upgrade checklist that includes driver compatibility validation and HSM/KMS verification steps.
[06:48] Liam: fine, please include that checklist.
[06:52] Priya: note on testing — we'll run a synthetic load that mirrors your traffic mix with long-prefix chats and validate both latency and token accuracy for fallbacks.
[07:05] Tom: how about observability — can we get token-level traces tied to request IDs?
[07:10] Jordan: yes we can provide token-level cost/latency breakdowns for the affected timeframe; linking to request IDs is possible if you provide the IDs.
[07:20] Michael: i'll compile request IDs and share them with jordan.
[07:24] Jordan: thanks.
[07:28] (crosstalk — background noise)
[07:40] Priya: on long-term reliability, recommend: 1) preflight driver checks and pinning, 2) staged canaries with traffic ramp, 3) KV cache adaptive policies and telemetry, 4) model-variant alignment testing for fallback paths, 5) stronger alerting for eviction + kernel errors correlation.
[08:05] Sara: who owns the canary policy change? is that redwood or aurora?
[08:12] Jordan: partnership — redwood will propose the policy and SE will help implement in your infra.
[08:20] Nadia: are there security implications for keeping audit logs longer? we might need extended retention for PCI/HIPAA checks.
[08:28] Liam: request retention extension for three months of operator logs for this window.
[08:33] Jordan: we can support extended retention for the incident window; will follow up with a plan.
[08:40] Tom: let's talk about runbook automation — can we automate detection by correlating certain GPU driver pop logs with KV eviction spikes and auto-signal a rollback?
[08:52] Priya: yes, we can add a monitoring rule: if eviction rate > X and kernel ABI errors > Y then trigger an operator alert and optionally throttle new allocations.
[09:05] Michael: on the postmortem doc, please include timeline with exact timestamps and the operator actions.
[09:11] Jordan: agreed we'll include detailed timeline in the doc we send.
[09:18] Avery: i'll own consolidation and distribution of the postmortem.
[09:22] Sara: can we also get a short SLA credit proposal? we did have an SLO breach.
[09:30] Jordan: i'll route that to finance/legal and get a proposal by the end of week.
[09:36] Liam: high level question — any changes to encryption or key access as part of the mitigation?
[09:41] Jordan: no changes to key material; mitigation was infra-level. we'll supply audit logs for verification.
[09:48] Tom: any follow-up QA on model output drift after fallback?
[09:52] Priya: we did spot checks on a corpus of 200 prompts; drift was minimal but we'll run a larger regression harness before enabling fallback permanently.
[10:08] Michael: ok let's confirm owners and due dates now.
[10:12] Jordan: Jordan will share postmortem and logs by 2025-11-22.
[10:16] Priya: SE will run a 20% canary with driver pinning and report perf by 2025-11-24.
[10:20] Michael: Aurora (Michael) will provide failing request IDs and SLO target doc by 2025-11-21.
[10:28] Nadia: schedule KV cache deep dive by 2025-11-25 — Nadia to coordinate.
[10:34] Avery: i'll circulate meeting notes and the link to the doc after this.
[10:40] Tom: thanks everyone. two quick items — can redwood provide a short security attestation for the incident?
[10:46] Jordan: yes, we'll include a statement of no data exfiltration and steps taken; legal can follow up if you need formal attestation.
[10:55] Sara: thanks, appreciate the quick mitigation.
[11:00] Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up with the doc and schedule the deep dive.

End of transcript.
